content:
The test image shows a tomato leaf with numerous small, circular spots scattered across the surface. Key features:
- Small lesions with lighter (tan/gray) centers and dark brown borders
- Multiple spots distributed across an otherwise green leaf
- Some yellowing visible around certain lesions
- No concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight/Target Spot)
- No water-soaked blotches (ruling out Late Blight)
- No webbing (ruling out Spider Mites)

The reference Septoria Leaf Spot images match closely — same small circular lesions with tan centers, dark perimeters, and distribution pattern across the leaf.

{"prediction": "Septoria_Leaf_Spot", "confidence": 0.88, "reasoning": "Leaf shows numerous small circular lesions with tan/gray centers and dark brown borders, scattered across a mostly green tomato leaf with some surrounding yellowing. This matches Septoria leaf spot's hallmark morphology — small (<1/8 in) lesions with lighter centers and dark perimeters — and aligns well with the reference collage. No concentric rings (Early Blight), no water-soaked blotches (Late Blight), no webbing (Spider Mites), and no shot-hole centers (Bacterial Spot)."}
